'''Emma J. Bunce''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|OBE}} (born 1975) is a British [[space physics|space physicist]] and Professor of Planetary Plasma Physics in the [[School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Leicester|School of Physics and Astronomy]] at the [[University of Leicester]].<ref name=gs/> She holds a [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]]. Her research is on the [[Magnetosphere of Saturn|magnetospheres of Saturn]] and [[Magnetosphere of Jupiter|Jupiter]]. She is [[principal investigator]] (PI) of the MIXS instrument on ''[[BepiColombo]]'', was deputy lead on the ''[[Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer]]'' proposal, and co-investigator on the ''[[Cassini–Huygens]]'' mission.

Bunce served as [[President of the Royal Astronomical Society]] from 26 June 2020<ref name=president_start_date>{{cite tweet|user=RoyalAstroSoc|name=Royal Astronomical Society|number=1276553465544822784|title=We are very excited to announce that Professor Emma Bunce has started her two year term as the new president of the Royal Astronomical Society!|date=26 June 2020}}</ref> to May 2022.<ref name=president_elected>{{cite web |last1=Hollis |first1=Morgan |title=Election results 2019: new RAS Council |url=https://ras.ac.uk/news-and-press/news/election-results-2019-new-ras-council |website=ras.ac.uk |publisher=Royal Astronomical Society |access-date=14 October 2019 |date=10 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://ras.ac.uk/news-and-press/news/election-results-2021-new-ras-council | title=Election results 2021: New RAS Council }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Bunce grew up in [[Worthing]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www2.le.ac.uk/departments/physics/people/emmabunce|title=Professor Emma Bunce — University of Leicester|last=tk74|website=www2.le.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=15 September 2018|archive-date=29 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180729012823/https://www2.le.ac.uk/departments/physics/people/emmabunce|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1989, she watched the ''[[Horizon (UK TV series)|Horizon]]'' documentary on [[Neptune]] with images taken by [[Voyager 2]] and was inspired to become a space scientist.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2016/07/05/nasa-spacecraft-junos-arrival-at-jupiter-prompts-british-scienti/|title=Nasa spacecraft Juno's arrival at Jupiter prompts British scientists' celebration: 'We're all feeling very relieved'|last=Knapton|first=Sarah|date=5 July 2016|work=The Telegraph|access-date=15 September 2018|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

She was educated at [[Davison High School]] (a C of E girls school) and [[Worthing College]] (a [[sixth form college]]), where she graduated in 1994.<ref name=":0" /> She studied physics with space science at the [[University of Leicester]] and earned her [[Master of Physics]] (MPhys) degree in 1998.<ref name=":0" />

In 1998, Bunce began her doctoral training with [[Stan Cowley]], investigating the [[magnetosphere of Jupiter]].<ref name=":0" /> Her thesis, ''Large-scale current systems in the Jovian Magnetosphere'', looked at the radial current systems of the middle magnetosphere of Jupiter.<ref>{{Cite thesis|degree=PhD|last=Bunce|first=Emma J.|date=2001|title=Large-scale current systems in the Jovian magnetosphere|url=https://lra.le.ac.uk/handle/2381/30647|hdl=2381/30647|website=le.ac.uk|publisher=University of Leicester|language=en|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.696997}}|oclc=505259820|access-date=15 September 2018|archive-date=16 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180916022736/https://lra.le.ac.uk/handle/2381/30647|url-status=dead}} {{free access}}</ref> She used data from [[Pioneer 10]], [[Pioneer 11]], [[Voyager 1]], [[Voyager 2]] and [[Ulysses (spacecraft)|Ulysses]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.org.uk/publications/181-education-a-careers/education-and-careers/competitions/63?task=view|title=The RAS - Blackwell Prize 2002|author=Anon|year=2002|website=www.ras.org.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> The interaction between Jupiter and the surrounding plasma environment is influenced by the magnetic field. On Jupiter, the plasma is mainly produced in the volcanic [[Moons of Jupiter|moon Io]].<ref name=":1" />

== Research and career ==
After her graduate studies, Bunce worked as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] investigating the Kronian [[magnetosphere of Saturn]] in preparation for [[Cassini–Huygens]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2003, Bunce was awarded a [[Particle Physics and Astronomy Research Council]] fellowship to study the [[magnetosphere of Saturn]].<ref name=":0" /> She continued to study Jupiter's polar auroral emissions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=T.|first1=Clarke, John|last2=Denis|first2=Grodent|last3=H.|first3=Cowley, Stan W.|last4=J.|first4=Bunce, Emma|last5=Philippe|first5=Zarka|last6=P.|first6=Connerney, John E.|last7=Takehiko|first7=Satoh|date=2004|title=Jupiter's aurora|journal=Jupiter. The Planet, Satellites and Magnetosphere|language=en|volume=1|pages=639|bibcode=2004jpsm.book..639C}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bunce|first=E. J.|date=2004|title=Jovian cusp processes: Implications for the polar aurora|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research|language=en|volume=109|issue=A9|pages=A09S13|doi=10.1029/2003ja010280|issn=0148-0227|bibcode=2004JGRA..109.9S13B|doi-access=free|hdl=2381/26050|hdl-access=free}}</ref> She was appointed to the faculty at the [[University of Leicester]] in 2005.<ref name=":0" />

Bunce was part of the [[Cassini–Huygens]] magnetometer team.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.org.uk/component/gem/?id=168|title=Royal Astronomical Society|website=www.ras.org.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> She was the first to analyse the UV aurorae of Saturn using the [[Hubble Space Telescope]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ras.org.uk/news-and-press/219-news-2012/2101-cassini-makes-simultaneous-measurements-of-saturns-nightside-aurora-and-electric-current-system|title=Cassini makes simultaneous measurements of Saturn's nightside aurora and electric current system|last=Massey|first=Robert|website=www.ras.org.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ras.org.uk/images/stories/awards/winners/2018/Chapman%20Medal%20-%20Emma%20Bunce.pdf|title=Citation for the 2018 RAS Chapman Medal|date=2018|website=RAS|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> The magnetosphere of Saturn rotates rapidly and plasma is produced ''via'' sputter of the icy moons.<ref name=":0" /> She monitored the magnetospheric currents of [[Saturn]] ''in situ'', identifying that there was a connection between the auroral oval and upward-directed field-aligned currents that flow near open and closed field lines.<ref name=":3" /> She observed the interaction of the solar wind with the [[magnetosphere of Saturn]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Jim|first=Wild|date=2009|title=RAS Awards 2009|journal=Astronomy & Geophysics|language=en|volume=50|issue=1|pages=1.34|doi=10.1111/j.1468-4004.2009.50134.x|issn=1366-8781|bibcode=2009A&G....50a..34.|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2009, she was elected to the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] Council<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ras.org.uk/news-and-press/68-news2009/1590-ras-council-2009-elections|title=RAS Council 2009 Elections Results|last=Elliott|first=David|website=www.ras.org.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> and delivered the society's [[Harold Jeffreys Lecture]].<ref name=":4" /> She discussed her work Jupiter-like [[aurora]]e found on [[Saturn]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Stallard|first1=Tom|last2=Miller|first2=Steve|last3=Melin|first3=Henrik|last4=Lystrup|first4=Makenzie|last5=Cowley|first5=Stan W. H.|last6=Bunce|first6=Emma J.|last7=Achilleos|first7=Nicholas|last8=Dougherty|first8=Michele|authorlink8=Michele Dougherty|date=2008|title=Jovian-like aurorae on Saturn|journal=Nature|language=En|volume=453|issue=7198|pages=1083–1085|doi=10.1038/nature07077|pmid=18563160|issn=0028-0836|bibcode=2008Natur.453.1083S|s2cid=4413780}}</ref>

She was promoted to reader in 2009 and professor in 2013.<ref name=":0" /> She organised a celebration of ten years of [[Cassini–Huygens]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ras.org.uk/component/gem/?id=297|title=Royal Astronomical Society|website=www.ras.org.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> She is the Principal Investigator of Bunce was elected [[President of the Royal Astronomical Society]] in 2019; she began her term on 26 June 2020<ref name=president_start_date/> and served two years.<ref name=president_elected/>

=== Public engagement ===
[[File:Professor Emma Bunce and Professor Stan Cowley FRS 02.jpg|thumb|right|Emma Bunce in 2016 with [[Stan Cowley]]]]

Bunce has delivered several popular science lectures.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eas.unige.ch/EWASS2018/plenary.jsp|title=EWASS 2018|last=Switzerland|first=Marc Türler, Dept. of Astronomy, University of Geneva|website=eas.unige.ch|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.widgety.co.uk/events/space-lectures-the-cassini-mission-to-saturn-13-years-of-discovery|title=Widgety|website=www.widgety.co.uk|language=en|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref> She has written for ''[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/emma-bunce-389758|title=Emma Bunce|website=The Conversation|date=11 July 2017 |language=en|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref>

She spoke at the ''[[New Scientist]]'' Live event in 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://live.newscientist.com/speakers/emma-bunce|title=Emma Bunce|work=New Scientist Live 2018|access-date=15 September 2018|language=en-GB|archive-date=16 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180916022926/https://live.newscientist.com/speakers/emma-bunce|url-status=dead}}</ref>

She was a guest on the [[BBC Radio 4]] programme ''[[The Life Scientific]]'' in June 2020.<ref>{{cite web |first=Jim|last=Al-Khalili|year=2020|title=Emma Bunce on the gas giants |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000jvxq |website=bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC]] |access-date=9 June 2020}}</ref>

===Honours and awards===
Bunce was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2024 New Year Honours]] for services to astronomy and science education.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=64269|supp=y|page=N12|date=30 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Awards for New Year 2024 |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/658daadd80a3bb000d9d05bd/NY24_-_GOV.UK_New_Year_Honours_List_2024.pdf |website=gov.uk |access-date=29 December 2023}}</ref>

Her other awards and honours include:
* 2020–2022 – [[President of the Royal Astronomical Society]]<ref name=president_elected/>
* 2018 – [[Chapman Medal]]<ref name=":3" />
* 2011 – [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] for Astronomy and Astrophysics<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/cn/news/grant-winners/419085.article|title=Grant winners|date=23 February 2012|work=Times Higher Education (THE)|access-date=15 September 2018|language=zh-hans}}</ref>
* 2009 – [[Harold Jeffreys Lecture]]<ref name=":4" /> 
* 2005 – [[European Geosciences Union|European Geophysical Union]] Young Talents in Geoscience Award<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.le.ac.uk/ebulletin-archive/ebulletin/news/press-releases/2000-2009/2004/09/nparticle-sps-hv4-v2c.html|title=University of Leicester - Star Prize for University Physicist|website=www.le.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=15 September 2018}}</ref>
* 2003 – [[French Academy of Sciences]] Prix Baron Nicolet award for space physics<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite journal|date=2004|title=Once a physicist...Lord Browne of Madingley|url=http://stacks.iop.org/2058-7058/17/i=11/a=47|journal=Physics World|language=en|volume=17|issue=11|pages=50|doi=10.1088/2058-7058/17/11/47|issn=2058-7058|url-access=subscription}}</ref> 
* 2002 – awarded the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] Blackwell Prize<ref name=":1" />
